Meeting header:

- Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Omar Ruiz (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Head of ML, Quantico), Ravi Patel (CTO), Samir Gupta (Lead Engineer)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Quantico Payments is evaluating Redwood for a pilot to power multilingual customer support and payment reconciliation automations. Key constraints: 32k+ context for multi-doc receipts, tool-calling to their payments APIs, strict data residency and audit logs, and a preference for private VPC for production. Discussion centered on open model choices (Mistral/Cohere style vs larger Open weights), implications of quantization and KV cache for latency and cost, and Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs. Action items and benchmarks agreed.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh afternoon, morning, wherever you are. this is Lena from Redwood, i run EMEA accounts but i'm filling in for the AE. we've got Omar from the SE team also. quick intros please?
[00:12] Maya Chen: hi I'm Maya, Head of ML at Quantico Payments. we handle the NLU pipeline for support and reconciliation. we've been doing some pilot models in-house and exploring how to scale.
[00:18] Ravi Patel: ravi here, CTO -- mostly to understand infra and compliance needs.
[00:22] Samir Gupta: samir, lead engineer on payments integration. we'll own the tool-calling layer.
[00:26] Omar Ruiz: great, thanks. quick agenda — model selection, context length needs, multilingual, tool calling, and deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private). we'll try to capture concrete next steps. sound okay?
[00:37] Maya Chen: yes. our top-level problem: we need an LLM-backed assistant that can ingest multi-page transaction bundles and customer chat history — typically 12–30 pages worth of docs per incident, so ~50k tokens in worst case. also need Spanish and Portuguese support, plus Japanese in a few markets.
[00:53] Lena Park: 50k tokens — got it. so you're looking for models with 32k or 64k and potentially 128k context?
[00:59] Maya Chen: ideally 64k, 128k would be nice for some reconciliations where we want full conversation + receipts. but we can trim; depends on cost.
[01:07] Omar Ruiz: okay. on the open-model side we typically recommend a few families — Mistral/Mistral-influenced variants for cost/throughput, some Cohere/Claude-style for instruction tuning, and larger Open models if you need the best instruction following at higher cost. also Redwood offers verified runtimes across those so you get consistent perf.
[01:28] Ravi Patel: when you say "verified runtimes" is that about latency or model behavior?
[01:33] Omar Ruiz: primarily runtime and performance profiles — latency SLAs are in Dedicated and Private modes. Hosted has SLOs but Dedicated gives reserved GPUs and predictable p99 latencies. model behavior — we do model cataloging and evals but we don't change weights.
[01:45] Samir Gupta: quick infra question — our security team will push for VPC/private deployment for production. what's the difference in data movement between Hosted and Private?
[01:54] Lena Park: good question. Hosted API never stores customer prompt content beyond ephemeral logs used for billing — though we can opt out. Dedicated is isolated hardware pools within Redwood and better for compliance. Private gives you a control plane in your VPC or an on-prem package — data stays in your network, and you manage networking/KMS.
[02:12] Maya Chen: and audit logs? we need detailed token-level audit for e-discovery.
[02:16] Omar Ruiz: Private and Dedicated both support enhanced audit logs; Private lets you ship logs to your SIEM directly. we support SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations.
[02:25] Maya Chen: good. back to models — tool calling: we need models to reliably call our payments processing APIs and a retrieval layer over our vector DB and SQL. how do you recommend we architect that?
[02:35] Omar Ruiz: most customers push tool calls through a middleware layer. Redwood supports structured tool-calling patterns — you can surface functions in the chat response. for reliability we suggest: 1) retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for facts, 2) deterministic tool-call step where model emits a function name + args, and 3) an orchestration layer to validate and execute that call.
[02:54] Samir Gupta: and is the function schema enforced? sometimes models hallucinate and try to call things they shouldn't.
[02:59] Omar Ruiz: yes you can validate the function output against JSON schema and we have rerouting/fallback policies so if a model tries an unsupported tool we can fallback to a safe path. also vocab: our runtime supports streaming so you can get early tool-call signals.
[03:12] Ravi Patel: ok cost vs latency — if we go 64k context, what's the cost delta between hosted and dedicated? and any recommendations for quantization?
[03:22] Omar Ruiz: relative numbers — hosted is usage-based; dedicated is committed capacity. for steady traffic dedicated usually lowers per-token cost by ~30–50% depending on pooling and batch efficiency. quantization to int8 or 4-bit can significantly reduce GPU memory and cost but you need to validate quality. we can run model-specific evals.
[03:37] Maya Chen: how reliable is prefix/KV caching for multi-turn conversations? our flows are very stateful.
[03:43] Omar Ruiz: Redwood's KV cache and prefix caching are optimized for multi-turn; we can cache embeddings and key-value activations to reduce recomputation. in Dedicated you get finer controls on cache eviction policies. sometimes the transcript shows 'K V cash' in auto-transcripts (laughs) — transcription, ha.
[03:58] Samir Gupta: are there documented regressions when switching quantized model variants? we can't risk dropping accuracy on reconciliation logic.
[04:05] Omar Ruiz: yes, that's why Redwood Optimize gives you quantization recommendations per workload. we run A/B evals with your prompt set. if we see regressions, we can fall back to FP16 variants or constrain quantization to certain layers.
[04:18] Maya Chen: multilingual — do we standardize on one model that handles Spanish/Portuguese/Japanese or run language-specific models?
[04:25] Omar Ruiz: tradeoffs: a single multilingual model simplifies deployments but may cost more and have uneven quality. language-specific smaller models can be cheaper and faster. many customers route by language at the routing layer — Redwood supports policy-based routing so you can send Spanish to a tuned 32k model and Japanese to a different variant.
[04:41] Ravi Patel: does Redwood support automatic routing by tenant or locale?
[04:45] Lena Park: yes, route by policy (latency, cost, region, tenant). you can pin tenants to dedicated pools if needed.
[04:51] Maya Chen: on the model front, we tested an open 32k model in-house but hit hallucinations on payment amounts when context truncated. how do you protect against that?
[05:00] Omar Ruiz: two approaches: first, stronger RAG with retrievals anchored to high-precision fields (e.g., exact receipts). second, use quality monitoring and regression alerts — Redwood ties evals to prompt sets and can trigger rollbacks if you see hallucination regressions after deploy.
[05:14] Samir Gupta: for the POC what would be a minimal setup?
[05:17] Lena Park: quick POC we typically do: 1) pick a 32k/64k model depending on your context, 2) hook up retrieval (vector DB + SQL), 3) implement sandboxed tool calling to your payments API, 4) run synthetic load to collect latency/cost numbers, and 5) run an eval on a holdout prompt set.
[05:37] Maya Chen: timeline — we want a pilot in ~6 weeks if possible. security signoff may add time.
[05:42] Ravi Patel: and budget? we have to evaluate dedicated commits vs hosted usage.
[05:46] Lena Park: we'll provide a TCO sketch — hosted run-rate vs a 3-month dedicated commit with projected throughput. Omar will include batch/caching assumptions.
[05:55] (brief crosstalk)
[05:58] Omar Ruiz: couple of gotchas — if you want 128k context it's more expensive and only a few model families currently support it well; we can show end-to-end latencies so you can decide where it's worth it. also if you do private on-prem, kernel and CUDA compat matrix matters — we'll coordinate with your infra team.
[06:15] Maya Chen: great. any blockers on our side for the POC?
[06:18] Samir Gupta: we'll need an API contract for tool calling and a sanitized dataset for evals. also we need detailed installation notes if we go private.
[06:25] Lena Park: we'll send an onboarding checklist and the security pack.
[06:28] Maya Chen: perfect. last question — do you have any customer references in payments?
[06:31] Lena Park: yes, we can share a couple — one fintech using dedicated pools for reconciliation and another using private VPC for EU-only data residency. we'll include anonymized case notes.
[06:42] Ravi Patel: ok let's recap the next steps.
[06:45] Lena Park: recap: Redwood sends SOC2/security docs and onboarding checklist (Lena) by 10/15; Omar runs a small latency/cost benchmark comparing hosted 32k vs dedicated 32k/64k using your sample prompts (Omar) by 10/17; Maya will share sample prompts and confirm pilot timeline (Maya) by 10/16; schedule technical deep dive for private deployment week of 10/20.
[07:05] Maya Chen: that works. thanks all.
[07:08] Samir Gupta: thanks.
[07:10] Ravi Patel: thanks everyone.
